All the lecture material is posted at the start of the semester so attendance is not mandatory, he records lectures anyways. However that also means every lecture is him reading off prewritten notes which yeah it can be boring but I found it helpful since he explains things in an intuitive way. I would definitely attend lecture but also use that time to take notes from his slides or textbook because if you just sit there and listen to him, you will fall asleep very quickly, he is very monotone. 

Homework was on expertta which does cost money and you are docked points for wrong answers but the textbook is free so, theres that. I got by fine without using the textbook at all and just using his notes as they are very comprehensive combined with his lectures. He also has solutions to study guides you can use to practice for exams and a formula sheet you get from day one. 

I don't know why people rag on him for being a little blunt at times, he won't hold your hand through the course but gives you the information to pass.

This class was pretty easy and Severson gives good resources to help you learn the material and prepare for exams. He gives a lot of real life examples in class which is cool and goes over fundamental things for each topic to help us better understand it. I think his lecture slides are pretty good and the examples we do together are really helpful to grasp the topic. 

The exams are harder than the quizzes but are still fair and don’t test content we haven’t learned.  

He’s nice and willing to help if you’re asking good questions and curious about physics!

I took this class over the summer and greatly benefited from not having to take other classes at the same time. Professor Severson is a pretty decent teacher. Class can be boring at times because he just reads off of prewritten notes but overall does a good job of explaining. 

There are 3 exams for this class. The first exam being weighted half as much as the last two. Overall, the exams are super fair and are basically problems from the lecture notes. Do well on the first two because the last one can be more challenging. 

Quizzes are super easy and are just meant to help your understanding. 

Homework was considerably harder than it needed to be. What is most frustrating is how the homework requires specific entry format. Also every wrong attempt takes points off so be certain with your submissions. 

Overall, this class was extremely fair and Professor Severson intends for you to do really well.

most of these reviews are pretty accurate, but one thing i disagree with is some people say that you need a good understanding of physics before entering the class. I took this class with no prior knowledge in physics at all, and I did fine. He drops the lowest exams and curves the grades pretty well so as long as you follow along with the class and make sure you understand whats happening on the homework this class is no harder than math140.

She is a pretty good professor. She doesn't make the lecture particularly boring but neither are they too exciting. I enjoyed her teaching style. She is both informative and tries to use her students to make the lectures flow in different direction, even if they are wrong. Exam wise: they definitely where challenging but never to the point that they were unfair or purposely tricky. She curved al the exams as well. Her office hours are VERY helpful, to the point that she will tell you the answers on the homeworks. Her TA was also very helpful and gives you great practice problems in discussion. I would recommend going to discussion even if its not mandatory mainly because its so helpful. If you are looking for a teacher that teaches to the syllabus and doesn't really pull any tricks, take Dr. Rice.

I read the reviews before taking this class and thought I wouldn't care about his monotone voice, but it actually is pretty bad. I try to pay attention to what he's saying, but it's impossible. I basically don't learn anything during the lecture, but you have to go since he doesn't post his notes. You also have to study a lot for this class; just going over the homework wasn't enough for me. You have to understand, and probably do some textbook practice. This is my first B in college, but I also think I am more of a memorization person, which doesn't really work in this class.

I do not get why people hate on this professor. Yes, what he goes over in class may be more simple than what can appear on exams. But that is the case with physics professors. They teach you formulas and how/when to apply them. Professors cannot teach you to problem solve. With that being said, I love Professor Buerhle. This class may be hard, but with practice, it is extremely doable. The curves are very hefty (usually around 20-25% a test if you are receiving the median score), the quizzes are take home and you get a week to do them, same thing goes for the homework. Additionally, lowest score on 1 out of the 3 exams is dropped, the lowest quiz grade is dropped, and a couple of your lowest homework grades are dropped.

he has got to be rage baiting me! If I could give a 0 star I most definitely would. Tell me why he's explaining the basics of a topic and then giving me jack all in the exam. Sure these exams are curved HEAVILY BECAUSE I WONDER WHY. MAYBE ITS THE FACT THAT THESE QUESTIONS ARE TESTING THE LIMITS OF OUR PATIENCE. If only we had a teacher teaching us anything more than surface level physics maybe we could keep up with his jack all questions on these exams. AND tell me why he's talking about sum "ion give out points to bump u for ur program even if it depends on it" because every time I take one of these exams I feel like I'm becoming more and more neurodivergent, it feels  like I'm genuinely losing my braincells. It's like taking tren without the tren and all of the side effects, matter of fact I think I'm gaining gyno from the amount of stress that is causing my hormonal imbalance.

Proffesor Belloni is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had, does that mean you should go to lecture, well it depends. If you are good at self studying or have already taken lectures never go to a single lecture they are pointless. Also don't go to discussion's you can do those in your room. You should go to the discussion before the test to ask questions on the test.

The test's are really HARD no lie. But he gives you 5 practice tests for each midterm and final. With those practice test I was able to get around 85 on the 1st 2 midterms and I didn't study for the third and got a 75. He drops 1 midterm, hw is easy, online quizes are easy.

ALSO GO TO OFFICE HOURS, hes really nice and he explains things much better then he does in lecture

I don't understand why this guy has less than 3 stars, he is really sweet and genuinely cares about his students passing. His lectures are a little disorganized but he posts everything online and gives plenty of practice and review. I feel so maternal towards him he's so nice. He gives free points for everything on exams. You literally get points for choosing an mcq answer. You might have to teach yourself a lot of the course, but it's pretty much fine if you do the practice he gives. I think his exams are fair and you can skip out on lecture, except I felt bad every time I slept through because he is really just trying his best :(. Please be kind to my guy Belloni he is just little belloni.

Professor Hu is a nice person, but his lectures felt impossible to follow. He would start problems without explaining what he was solving for, struggled to actually answer student questions, and if you didn't sit in the front it was hard to see what he was writing on the chalkboard. If you don't come into this class without some sort of physics background you will struggle.

On the plus side, exams were difficult but fair. They were very similar to examples he did in lecture, so definitely go to lecture even if you don't know what's happening. I learned more about the actual concepts from my TA and the textbook, but I studied his examples to prepare for exams.
awesome professor, gives a lot of resources to practice with and the homeworks are pretty helpful. definitely take her if you have the chance

Very sweet guy; you can tell he likes physics and cares about his students but his exams were difficult and lectures were generally unhelpful. He barely uses numbers in exam questions (mostly conceptual based) which made them really confusing. Homeworks and quizzes were manageable (they had numbers in the questions & made more sense than midterms) but a lot of this course was me teaching myself the content. Lectures were all over the place and were not super engaging. Somewhat typical for a math-based class at UMD but I did expect better.

He is a good professor, 100% better than any other professors that teach PHYS161. I like his lecture style; he tries to be casual, dropping some curse words while lecturing. I didn’t go to his lecture after 3 weeks and studied only like 3 to 4 days before each exam. Homework is due every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, and participation is due after every lecture. He has online quizzes that are usually easy; some questions are hard and need critical thinking. Exams are harder than homework and quizzes, so do study and try to understand the concepts and how you can manipulate formulas to answer questions. Even though exams are hard, he curves like crazy and really boosts your grade. TBH, I kind of like his exam style because it pushes you to your limit, and he understands that, which is why he curves every exam like crazy. If you can’t make the average on exams, then I believe you need to reconsider your major or the choice of courses you take in the future. He is really understanding, checks his emails, and corrects grades if he makes any mistakes. Exams are 30%, homework is 20%, quizzes 15%, final 30%, and participation 5%. There are 3 exams, and the lowest gets dropped, which is usually the 3rd one. Really try hard on the first 2, as they are much easier than the 3rd one. Take him if you can.

He is a very nice professor who you can tell is passionate about what he is teaching; however, he is not the best teacher. He sometimes gives examples that are based on Physics 2 or 3 concepts, which confuses us a lot.

As for his exams, they always have at least one trick question meant to test how well you can apply concepts to an unseen problem, so if you aren’t good at that, you will probably struggle on exams. His averages were usually in the mid-60s, with the final being in the low-70s. The only thing I didn’t like is that for the final, you could only use formulas that appear in the back of the textbook chapters for your formula sheet, so you didn’t have much freedom with that.

On the bright side, he does drop your lowest exam score and applies a curve at the end of the course.

Pretty good teacher I neve took any physics before and ended with a B. I am a pretty average student who has failed a class before, but do spend tons of time studying.  His exams 2 and 3 can be a bit difficult but he curves all exams to compensate for it all. Yes the lectures will only be general stuff, so do some Khan academy, watch crash course(I found this personally super helpful), or read the book whatever floats your boat.  Homework's can be long but try not to use AI they will help you with the concepts and problem solving even though they can cook your brain.

He deserves almost none of the hate he gets. It's a hard class but my final grade was curved, he counted the last 3 homework as extra credit (there were 33 total so this was a free 110% in homework category if you got an 100 on the homework that gives you 5 attempts per question), and graded the exams super lightly. Everyone else here is just salty they failed a (very easy) class, just wait until you get into higher level engineering classes, he looks like an angel in comparison. I had several email conversations with him, all of which he was very kind and understanding in. From rescheduling quizzes for me when I was sick (weekly canvas quiz due Sundays) to helping me with issues in ExpertTA. I only take one star away because his lectures are almost useless, and you will learn a lot more by doing practice problems, though he does explain that quite clearly. I would absolutely choose him over the other physics professors based on what I have heard from friends in the other professors classes. He finds a way to make the class fun, gives tons of old practice exams that are almost identical, and manages to make the "weed out" class pretty easy. I'd say I spent three hours a week on the class and still got a B-. For sure the best physics professor/teacher I've had though. He loves to help students understand if you go ask him questions, and his TA's are wonderful. Just watch out for his exams, and this semester for the final with little warning he told us we could only use formulas from the textbook, which I did not appreciate. On the midterms we were welcome to do anything we wished on our formula sheet. Just prepare for his exams, he drops your lowest midterm, and he curves. Wish I could take him for 260. I do have a unique perspective here though, because I am a sophomore who was in this class. I'd bet a lot of the negative reviews are freshmen in their first semester who have not experienced a college course and realized that this is how they all are.

This class was one of the root causes of my mental distress. I did not have much prior knowledge of physics 1 content, but the way this professor taught made it tremendously more difficult for no reason. This did not help in getting me to enjoy the class content.

Dr. Hu clearly knew a great deal about this field, but did not know how to convey it effectively to students. He assumed everyone wanted him to go faster and that the content was “too easy.” He would start problems without finishing them or would jump to answers out of nowhere. He would only use variables (no numbers), which made deciphering his work even harder. I will also not forget that he did not provide practice tests or any in-class practice/review for midterms.

Speaking of midterms, there were 2 of them, and they were each extremely conceptual and graded harshly. The averages were always low. The same applies to the final. 

The homework was graded for accuracy on the Expert TA site, which was super glitchy. Overall, I thought them to be tedious and difficult. I will also note that each question gave you 5 tries and a couple of hints. One homework was dropped at the end.

In general, one could argue that you learned more through the textbook readings, which tells you something since I thought the textbook was awful. YouTube and online academic sites are what helped me the most for this course. 

My discussion section was quite unpleasant. I did not like how the TA would write a problem on the blackboard and then would give us time to think about it and solve it, and then would go over it at a rapid speed; this method just took up so much of our time, stripping us of the opportunity to try other types of problems. I felt like the TA could have also done more review of the class’s main themes for prep before quizzes and tests. There were bi-weekly quizzes that he wrote himself and were challenging. One was dropped at the end.

The one redeeming aspect that I will forever praise for this class is that there was a huge curve at the end (at least 10%). I am greatly thankful for it, and for that reason, my rating is slightly higher than what I initially wanted to give and the rating for the rest of the course.

Dr. Belloni is incredibly kind and understanding. His accent can make lectures unclear, but he answers all questions and doesn't make you feel stupid for asking them. He's very approachable after class and responds to all emails in a timely manner. Well organized- provides all slides and notes from class. The pacing is fast, but physics is always tough (took ap physics c in hs). He definitely curved and offered a little optional extra credit for completing extra homework sets. You unfort have to pay $35 for ExpertTA (homework website), but he generously gives you hints and ~5 attempts per question.

Very nice and kind professor. He is whole hearted and is willing to make sure everyone gets help. Professor Hu is very involved in proving why physics works. It is kind of difficult to understand if you don’t do a ton of examples on your own. Sometimes his explanations make no sense, and he commonly mistakes any questions directed towards an example with another example on the board. His tests are basically the examples done in class. It does not teach any students how to apply concepts learned in class to different scenarios. The tests don’t efficiently test knowledge. The final is difficult without proper preparation though, as another professor makes it (That was the case this year at least). Do not rely on just the notes for the final. Do the practice finals for the final exam. I would not recommend taking him if this is your first time taking physics though. Overall he is not a bad professor.

I took Dr. Severson's class over the summer. He definitely can be kind of blunt, but he's overall a nice person and will help out however he can if you reach out first. Homework was a little irritating because it took percentages off for incorrect submissions.

I really liked him. He kept the lectures interesting and fun which is hard for a class like physics. He is really sus about the curve, cause we did not have one the entire class up until the final grade. The midterms were not super difficult. The final was pretty difficult but he ended up doing a final grade curve and my grade went from a B+ to an A. Overall would definitely recommend to any freshman needing to take PHYS161.

I really liked having him. He kept the lectures funny and interesting which is hard for such a boring class. The midterms were not super difficult. The final was pretty hard but nothing crazy. He was really sus about the curve cause there was not one the entire time. He ended up curving our final grades and my grade went from a B+ to an A.

Buehrle is not that bad in spite of the reviews posted here. I always felt like what he went over during class was way more simple than what was covered on the exams. Even the previous exams that he provided for us (4 for each exam as well as the final which he created) felt easier than the actual exam for some reason. Other people in the class felt the same way. His lectures did not feel like enough, you always had to get supplemental knowledge from somewhere else, however all of his lectures are recorded. He is a nice enough professor. There are weekly quizzes worth 15% with lowest dropped, homework on expertTA worth 20% with lowest couple dropped (HW is somewhat relevant to the course and it will help you gain a greater understanding but the questions are not similar to exam questions in terms of style), after every lecture there are a one question quiz for participation worth 5% with lowest ones dropped, 3 midterms worth 30% with lowest dropped, and final which is cumulative worth 30% which he creates on his own. As someone who does not have prior physics experience, this class was tough (I took physics online in the summer in HS). I attended most of the lectures and went to the physics course center for help often. What did not help was the TA. First of all, the discussion was too short. it always felt rushed, with him trying to cover the past weeks topics and then asking us to attempt 3 problems with barely enough time for him to go over any of them, least of all getting help. If the discussion was longer and the TA a tad bit better, I would do much better in this course. I did very poorly on the exams, just like everybody else. He curved the hell out of them which is the only reason he's getting 4 stars and I managed to get a B-. I would recommend spamming problems from the textbook to study and watch organic chem tutor.

Great guy, but not the strongest lecturer. Always talked too fast for himself and often went on interesting tangents not really related to the content. Reads slides a lot but really tries to expand on them or provide a demonstration of the effect, or show how an equation is derived. Always willing to pause the lectures and answer questions to ensure that students understood. Homework wasn't bad with five chances per problem. Tests were a challenge, but doing well on the homework and simply studying aids in that. Generous curve, I was expecting around a C+/B- but ended with a B+ despite averaging under 70 for the midterms.

Learned literally nothing
He curves all the exams like crazy but if his exams weren't so hard in the first place, he wouldn't need to curve as hard.

Buehrle seems like a really nice dude, and he's super funny. As for his teaching ability, I feel like he's too smart to understand why we are struggling to understand this beginner-level physics material. I took this class having 0 physics experience; I didn't even take algebra-based physics in high school. Luckily, I took Calc III the semester before taking this class, which helped A LOT, and is probably the reason I did well in this class. I will say, to me, his first exam was fair, but the second and third exams got a little rocky. Luckily, there is one dropped exam (I still do not understand exam 3 material) and a heavy curve. I mainly learned by watching YouTube videos and taking practice exams, not from lectures tbh, but at the end of the day, this class is doable. Also, since his midterms are on the more difficult side, the final, which is also curved, will feel comparatively more doable.

Her lectures are nice; they are energetic and engaging. It is also nice that she drops your lowest midterm. However, her quizzes are bad, as in messy, and you get a short time limit for them. You do not really have time to check your work and none of them are dropped. The sad part is, they make up 15% of your score. Moreover, the homework site she uses is garbage- it barely gives any feedback, the hints are useless, and the homework will mark you wrong over using t instead of delta(t). Even more so, if you forfeit a question or get it wrong too many times, the site will not explain how to properly approach the problem.

tldr; nice teacher, good (but FAST) lectures, drops a midterm, but her quizzes and homeworks are horrendous and do not provide any proper feedback.

He is a very monotone speaker making lectures very boring but his style of teaching is very good. Midterms can be tricky but homework and quizzes aren’t a problem. Be prepared to do a lot of studying tho

Great guy, and passionate lecture which made the class surprisingly engaging. He moves a little quick, but has a lot of enthusiasm and is pretty funny. His office hours were very helpful, and he was always glad to help. His midterms were pretty difficult but not too bad, and the curve is incredible.
Very good teacher. She gives all the tools to succeed.

Belloni was very enthusiastic and nice but he isn’t fit for such a simple class. His lectures are surface level while his exams are much more complex. I found that doing the challenging textbook problems and reviewing problems covered in discussion is the best way to prepare for the exams. If you do this from the start then you’re certain to get an A with all his curves and the one dropped midterm exam grade.

great professor, quick but easy to follow lectures and plenty of examples worked through in class. she provides about a decade's worth of past exams to go through (with solutions as well). her exams are slightly harder than expected, but nothing bad at all
He is AWFUL! Pick a different section if he is your TA!
Just save yourself the trouble and pick someone more predictable and experienced with teaching like Hailu. She also uses Hailu's old exams as prep and switches up on the question type.
